summary.prose: When a stage is reassigned in the tracker, the previous owner's next changing action is refused as today and now also offers to park: the draft artifacts and a checkpoint of the run (plan, step outputs, next step) are committed to a handoff branch named from the repo's branch pattern, pushed, and noted on the stage's issue. The new assignee resumes with one command: the daemon fetches the branch, restores the files and rebuilds the run on their machine, continuing at the next unfinished step. If no checkpoint exists, for instance after a lost machine, resume rebuilds from the committed artifact files and restarts only the stage that has no artifact.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: A daemon-side team gate over a synchronous, capability-declaring tracker port (alternative a1). The port (sc1) is the only way the workflow library talks to a tracker; GitHub is its first adapter, made by extracting the existing GitHub code (src/workflow/tracker, the issue calls in tracker-auto.ts, and the create and close calls in src/workflow/bugfix/tracker.ts) behind it. sc1 is the one tracker abstraction: the unbuilt tracker-tool design (LLD-38436e90625a83a2-S001) is not built as a second abstraction and is superseded or amended by s1's LLD. The policy (sc2) is read from the remote default branch and says which stages need signoff, whether claims are enforced, the claim units and the administrators. The artifact's tracker record keeps every existing meta.tracker field exactly as it is and gains additive per-unit data, plus an optional meta.revision (sc3). The team gate (sc4) takes a guarded action and returns an outcome. Signoff is a separate record (sc5) that never changes meta.review or approvedAt. Syncing tracker status on git pull and push, and the issue-status read it needs, are deferred with the later-tracker work to a define extend and are not part of this HLD.

consumedContracts.name: Team gate, claim state, gate outcome, refusal error and completion hook
consumedContracts.purpose: The single gate for guarded actions in the daemon-owned workflow library, the claim state read live from the tracker, the outcome type, the typed refusal error that leaves approval, the review-fix decision that both review paths (verdicts.ts and run-artifact.ts) consult, and a completion hook that s5 ships unregistered and s7 registers. The gate derives the acting user itself through the port, so no caller signature changes. Owned by s5; s4 supplies issue creation which the gate calls for the no-issue outcome.

boundary.internal: Parking a draft on a handoff branch, the issue note, resuming from committed files, and reconstructing in-flight workflow state from committed artifacts instead of the opaque token.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: The GitHub adapter built by extracting src/workflow/tracker (including the existing signed-in-user read, ghCurrentLogin, behind whoAmI), the issue calls in tracker-auto.ts and the create and close calls in src/workflow/bugfix/tracker.ts behind the port; the gh command wrapper with its 10-second timeout; contract tests; detection of a missing tool or sign-in. The port receives the needed capabilities as an argument, so s1 does not read the policy. Reconciliation: the unbuilt tracker-tool design LLD-38436e90625a83a2-S001 (docs/standalone/add-add-items-tracker-setting-have-E2026100638436e90/S001/LLD.md) is not built as a second abstraction; sc1 is the one tracker abstraction and s1's LLD supersedes or amends that LLD, once its conflicting approval status is settled. Syncing tracker status on git pull and push, and an issue-status read on the port, are deferred to the define extend.

Reading the policy file from the remote default branch ref, the cached last-fetched copy and the offline rule, finding the first default-branch commit that carried the policy file, the starter policy and the team setup command.

The repo-scoped kind of row in the shared settings catalog whose reads and writes go to the per-repo map in github.json read by resolveGithubConfig; its rendering in VS Code, JetBrains and the terminal client; read-only display of policy values. Shares the single store with s1's target resolution.

Shared issue-creation code refactored out of autoPushEpicOnHld, autoPushStoryOnLld and autoPushTasksOnPlan, find-by-label dedupe for Story and Task issues, forcing Task issues on in team mode, daemon-side triggering when a draft is first written, the terminal approve path kept as manual fallback, the inventory and classification of artifact write paths (including the two writeFileSync writers, and both verdicts.ts and run-artifact.ts as content writes when auto-fixes change the body), the single content-write helper and the revision minting, the bypass test that also detects raw writeFileSync on artifact paths, and the rule that an artifact without meta.revision reads as revision 0.

The team gate and its call sites (daemon step entry points and approveArtifactByJsonPath), the acting-user read through the port, claim and release commands, live assignee reads, the guarded-action list (code-review and analyze are never guarded; review is never refused), the report-only review for a non-holder through the review-fix decision on both review paths (verdicts.ts and run-artifact.ts), the typed TeamGateRefusedError, its handling beside ReviewBlockedError in approveWorkflowTarget and its formatting in the terminal client's approve case in src/cli/command.ts, the no-issue outcome handling, administrator release, and the declaration of the completion hook, shipped unregistered.

Opening the signoff request with the chosen artifacts, prerequisite checks for model review and local approval, registering the completion hook to produce the awaiting-signoff outcome, the on-demand completion check, automatic release of the claim on completion, recording sign-off together, grandfathering of artifacts approved before the policy anchor, and the separate display of signoff.
Revision of an open request: re-run of local approval, push to the same request, discarding an earlier completion, refusing non-holders.
Private implementation of s9: Keep tracker issues and status in step with the work without a manual step

nonFunctional.performance: Each guarded action makes at most two live reads through the port (the signed-in user and the assignee); every tracker command has a 10-second timeout, after which the action is refused with the reason. A repo without a policy makes no tracker call.
nonFunctional.security: Policy is read only from the remote default branch ref and is not locally overridable; enforcement lives in the daemon-owned workflow library (k1); no tracker secrets are stored by insrc, sign-in stays with the tracker's CLI; administrators come only from the policy.
nonFunctional.observability: Every gate outcome other than allowed is logged with unit, action and reason; port failures carry their kind (missing-tool, missing-signin, unreachable, rejected).
nonFunctional.durability: Claim, issue and signoff state live in the tracker and in committed artifact files; the in-memory step state stores (100 entries, 1 hour) are not relied on for handoff. Artifact writes stay atomic through the existing helper.

dataModelChanges.details: Written to .insrc/handoff/<unit-key>.json on the handoff branch only. Fields: schemaVersion (1), unit (UnitRef without repoPath), parkedBy, parkedAt, sourceHead (commit the parker was on), stage (WorkflowStepStage), runId, epicKey, intent (workflow, focus, params), executor (ExecutorState: plan, nextStepIndex, stepOutputs, pause) when stage is awaiting_llm_step, stepOutputs when awaiting_synthesize, artifactPaths (repo-relative files parked with it). Restoring it never trusts paths: each must be a file under the unit's own artifact paths.
offerPark was always false. It is now true when the registered park-offer provider returns true for (repo, unit, actor). The type is unchanged.
A held-by-other outcome with offerPark true appends the park command to the reason, so every client that prints the refusal also prints the offer.

The row in the shared settings catalog gains a default (insrc/handoff/{type}-{id}) and loses its not-used-yet note; the grammar's placeholders stay id, slug, type. The validator and the settings clients pick the change up from the one row (k6).
One comment body: a marker line '<!-- insrc:handoff -->', the branch name, the checkpoint commit, who parked and the stage. Posted through the port's comment capability; nothing reads it back.

interactionWithShared.howDetails: Reads GateOutcome and TeamGateRefusedError unchanged. resumeStage asks teamGate with action 'author' (which claims an unassigned unit through the add-only assignment). parkDraft reads the holder through the same gate read and refuses when the actor holds the unit. The only addition to sc4 is registerParkOfferProvider, proposed as an amendment, so offerPark can be set without a cycle.

errorCases.scenario: Park is requested while the actor holds the unit
errorCases.detection: parkDraft reads the holder through the gate and finds the actor's own login
errorCases.response: Return ok:false with 'you hold this stage; there is nothing to hand over'. Nothing is written
errorCases.userImpact: A clear refusal instead of a branch for work the user still owns

errorCases.scenario: The unit has no issue or no holder (nobody to hand over to)
errorCases.detection: The gate outcome for the read is no-issue or the holder is null
errorCases.response: Return ok:false naming the reason; an unassigned unit is claimed and continued, not parked
errorCases.userImpact: The user is told to claim rather than park

errorCases.scenario: Nothing to park: no live run and no draft artifact for the unit
errorCases.detection: listLiveRuns returns empty and the unit's artifact paths are absent or unchanged from HEAD
errorCases.response: Return ok:false 'no draft or run to hand over'

errorCases.scenario: Branch name breaks the grammar after filling placeholders
errorCases.detection: handoffBranchName validates against the branchPattern row grammar
errorCases.response: Return ok:false with the grammar rule broken; no git command runs
errorCases.userImpact: The user fixes the pattern in settings

errorCases.scenario: Git fails while parking (not a repository, detached HEAD, hook rejects the commit, push rejected, remote unreachable)
errorCases.detection: runGit returns ok:false for the failing step
errorCases.response: Stop at that step, remove the local handoff branch and temporary worktree it created, keep the live run state untouched, and report the git message with the step name. A rejected push because the branch moved reports that someone else parked first
errorCases.userImpact: The draft is not lost: the run stays in the daemon and the working files stay where they are

errorCases.scenario: The issue note cannot be posted
errorCases.response: Keep the pushed branch, return ok:true with noted:false and the failure kind, and print the branch name so the user can tell the new owner
errorCases.userImpact: Handoff works but the issue lacks the pointer until the user retries or says it

errorCases.scenario: Resume finds a checkpoint with an unknown schemaVersion, a unit that does not match, or a path outside the unit's artifact paths
errorCases.detection: Parsing and validating the checkpoint before anything is written
errorCases.response: Return refused with the specific field; no file is restored and no run state is saved
errorCases.userImpact: The new owner is told the checkpoint is unusable and may restart the stage from the committed artifacts

errorCases.scenario: Resume would overwrite uncommitted local changes to the same artifact files
errorCases.detection: git status --porcelain on the files to restore is non-empty
errorCases.response: Return refused naming the files; nothing is touched
errorCases.userImpact: The new owner commits or stashes first

errorCases.scenario: Resume cannot fetch the handoff branch
errorCases.detection: git fetch of the deterministic branch name fails
errorCases.response: Distinguish a missing branch (no checkpoint: fall back to restart from committed artifacts) from a network or permission failure (refused with the git message)
errorCases.userImpact: A lost-machine takeover works without the branch; a network failure is not mistaken for a missing branch

errorCases.scenario: Restoring a checkpoint whose upstream artifacts changed since it was parked
errorCases.detection: Compare the upstream artifact revisions recorded at park time with the current files
errorCases.response: Return refused with 'the upstream moved since this draft was parked' and the restart option, because step outputs were computed against older input
errorCases.userImpact: The new owner redoes the stage on current input instead of resuming a stale one

alternativesConsidered.name: Park-time checkpoint on a handoff branch
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Parking writes the run's executor state to a checkpoint file, commits it with the draft artifacts to a handoff branch, pushes it, and notes it on the issue; resuming loads the checkpoint into a fresh run.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Add a handoff module under src/workflow/team that owns a HandoffCheckpoint record written to .insrc/handoff/<unit-key>.json. Park names the branch from branchPattern, creates it from the current HEAD, writes the checkpoint and the unit's draft artifacts, commits, pushes, and adds one comment to the unit's issue naming the branch and the checkpoint commit. The gate sets offerPark true on held-by-other when the acting user has a live run for the unit or an uncommitted draft artifact for it. Resume fetches the branch, validates the checkpoint, saves its executor state into the daemon's store and returns the next step turn. With no checkpoint, resume falls back to the committed artifacts alone.
pros: No per-step network traffic; one push at park time
Reuses ExecutorState, runGit and the port's comment capability
cons: Does not help when the machine is lost before parking
Creates and pushes a branch from the user's checkout
A checkpoint needs a schema version and a refusal on mismatch

alternativesConsidered.name: Artifacts-only park, restart the stage on resume
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Parking commits whatever artifact files exist and notes the branch; resuming always restarts the stage from its first step, seeded with the parked draft as context.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Park commits the unit's draft artifact files to the handoff branch, pushes, and comments the branch on the issue. No executor state is stored. Resume checks out the files and starts the stage again from step one with the existing artifact as the starting draft.
pros: Smallest change: no new on-disk schema
One resume path for both parked and lost-machine cases
cons: Fails ac27 for a stage parked mid-run
Gives the new owner no signal of what was done
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Smallest, but it violates ac27 for the common mid-run case, which is the point of the Story.

alternativesConsidered.name: Continuous checkpoint to a per-unit handoff branch
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Every completed step of a claimed unit writes the checkpoint and pushes it to the unit's handoff branch, so parking is only a note and a lost machine loses at most one step.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Extend a1 so the workflow-step phases, after each step output is stored, write the checkpoint file and the draft artifacts and commit them to a dedicated handoff branch through a separate worktree, pushing in the background with a short deadline. Parking then adds the issue note and a final push.
pros: Satisfies ac28 in its strongest reading
Parking is cheap and cannot fail on a dirty working tree
cons: Adds a commit and a network push to every step of every team run
Needs a managed worktree, background pushes and branch rights for every developer
Largest surface: changes the hot path of all four workflow-step phases
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Strongest on ac28, but it commits and pushes on every step of every team run and needs a managed worktree and branch rights for all developers, beyond this Story's boundary.

openQuestions: ac28 says the new assignee 'redoes only the unfinished step'. Committed artifact files exist only per finished stage, so after a lost machine a half-run stage restarts from its first step (completed stages are never redone). Accept stage-level redo, or adopt continuous checkpointing (a3), which commits and pushes on every step of every team run?
